input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: Subsection 11.3 is the only verification/investigation right binding Customer (there is no separate audit clause; searches for audit, inspection, records and verification return nothing else). It lets IBM investigate Customer's use of the Services and Content for AUP compliance with no frequency cap, no advance notice of the investigation itself (the notice in p0137 applies only before IBM restricts access or removes Content), and no cost allocation, while p0138 obliges Customer to hand over all relevant information on request. Unlimited and unannounced verification is walk-away territory and fails the fallback on frequency, notice and cost, so we added the three fallback limits by the shortest insertion rather than rewriting the clause. Preferred extras (independent auditor, off-site, 5% threshold, no system access) are not pursued at this level.

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.

ops.text: IBM may investigate potential violations under this Subsection 11.3 no more than once per year, and only after giving Customer at least fifteen (15) days' notice. IBM will bear the costs of each such investigation unless it reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's investigation right in 11.3 is currently unlimited and unannounced, so we added our fallback audit limits: one investigation per year, fifteen days' notice, and IBM bearing the cost unless an underpayment over 10% is found.
proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice and cost limits to IBM's investigation right in 11.3
